title: Why are some animals black and white?

vocabulary.meaning: colours or patterns that help an animal blend into its surroundings
examples: Zebra stripes may not work as simple camouflage.
Camouflage helps some animals avoid predators.

vocabulary.meaning: the natural colours and patterns on an animal or plant
examples: Scientists study how animal colouration evolves.
Black-and-white colouration can have several possible functions.

vocabulary.meaning: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
examples: Camouflage can make prey harder for predators to see.
The bird is an important predator in the ecosystem.

vocabulary.meaning: an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
examples: The pattern may confuse predators chasing their prey.
Small mammals are common prey for the owl.

vocabulary.meaning: the gradual change of species over many generations
examples: Animal colour patterns can develop through evolution.
Natural selection is a major mechanism of evolution.

vocabulary.meaning: a characteristic that helps an organism survive or reproduce
examples: Thick fur is an adaptation to cold climates.
Scientists debate which adaptation explains zebra stripes.

vocabulary.meaning: a repeated arrangement of colours, shapes, or markings
examples: Each zebra has a unique stripe pattern.
The bird's black-and-white pattern is easy to recognise.

vocabulary.meaning: an organism that lives on or in another organism and benefits at its expense
examples: Some colour patterns may reduce attacks from parasites.
Ticks are common external parasites.

vocabulary.meaning: the process of controlling body temperature
examples: Researchers have proposed that stripes may help temperature regulation.
Animals use several methods of temperature regulation.

vocabulary.meaning: the process in which useful inherited traits become more common over generations
examples: Natural selection can shape an animal's appearance.
Different environments create different pressures for natural selection.
